strengths: Novel application of intrinsic dimensionality to analyze reasoning strategies, with theoretically grounded motivation from MDL principle and information theory
Strong empirical correlations (0.93 for 4B, 0.75 for 1B) substantially outperforming baselines (length 0.31, KL divergence -0.17, token perplexity 0.82), with statistical significance p < 0.01

Comprehensive experimental validation including: 14 diverse reasoning strategies, 2 model scales, 6 test splits (1 in-distribution + 5 OOD), robustness across threshold choices (0.72-0.94 correlation range)
Thorough reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters, configuration selection algorithm, complete reasoning strategy examples, and dataset documentation

Insightful secondary findings: Executed PoT achieves lowest ID with best OOD performance; larger models compress effective reasoning more efficiently; ineffective strategies show amplified ID on larger models
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 2-3 Pareto frontiers) and well-structured appendix demonstrating rigorous experimental methodology
weaknesses: Significant limitation to single task domain (GSM8K math problems): unclear whether findings generalize to code, logical reasoning, knowledge-intensive QA, or other reasoning task types, constraining claims about reasoning effectiveness broadly

Establishes correlation but not causality: cannot determine if low ID enables better generalization or merely correlates with other factors like structural coherence; post-hoc explanations of baseline metric failures suggest possible specification hunting

LoRA-based operationalization not validated against true intrinsic dimensionality: structured LoRA projections differ fundamentally from unstructured random projections in original work (Li et al., 2018); no ablation on which weight matrices drive effective reasoning

Limited statistical power with only 14 reasoning strategies for correlation analysis; visual inspection reveals outliers (Critical CoT: ID=104.12M but Overall=37.52%) with sensitivity to outliers not reported

Computational impracticality for practitioners: requires 20-30 fine-tuning runs per strategy to compute ID; total computational cost not discussed, limiting real-world applicability for reasoning strategy selection

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: no analysis of which structural properties (decomposition, variable naming, verification) reduce ID; distractors' effect on ID (output length vs semantic noise) unexplored; no investigation of most critical transformer components

Limited actionability: demonstrates effective reasoning reduces ID but provides no guidance on designing strategies to minimize ID, using ID as training objective, or computing metric without expensive fine-tuning sweeps

Threshold selection methodology concerns: using fixed absolute threshold τ justified for comparison fairness, but choice of 90% epoch-1 training accuracy is somewhat ad-hoc; alternative normalization schemes not explored

strengths: Strong empirical results with remarkably consistent correlations (0.93 for 4B, 0.75 for 1B) across model sizes
Intrinsic dimensionality substantially outperforms baselines: 0.93 vs 0.82 (token perplexity), 0.31 (length), -0.17 (KL divergence)
Rigorous experimental design with comprehensive robustness analysis across threshold choices (0.72-0.94 correlations), multiple model sizes, and diverse reasoning strategies (14 total)
Generalizes across reasoning types: perfect 1.00 correlation on both algorithmic and cognitive reasoning tasks
Important ablations demonstrating sensitivity to data correctness (500× ID increase with noisy training data)
Well-motivated novel application: inverting standard intrinsic dimensionality setup to compare reasoning strategies rather than models
Clear presentation with informative Pareto frontier visualizations and comprehensive implementation details
Practical insights: Executed PoT consistently achieves lowest ID and best OOD performance; larger models compress effective strategies more efficiently
weaknesses: Limited practical applicability: Computing intrinsic dimensionality requires 20-30 fine-tuning runs per strategy; token perplexity achieves 0.82 correlation with negligible computational cost, raising questions about cost-benefit justification

Model and domain specificity: All experiments on Gemma-3 only; no validation on LLaMA, Mistral, or other architectures; evaluation heavily skewed toward math reasoning (GSM8K-dominated), with limited Reasoning Gym validation

Strong dependency on training data quality: Results only hold when training data is carefully filtered for correctness; metric breaks with mixed correct/incorrect chains, limiting real-world applicability

Correlation vs. causation: Paper establishes strong correlation but doesn't rigorously establish why lower intrinsic dimensionality improves generalization; MDL principle connection is stated but underexplored

Threshold selection concerns: Choice of epoch-1 maximum accuracy as threshold is reasonable but somewhat arbitrary; while robustness is demonstrated (Table 3), the need to justify this choice suggests potential brittleness

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: What specific properties of reasoning chains lead to low intrinsic dimensionality? Paper doesn't decompose this; no guidance on how to modify strategies to reduce ID
Technical proxy concerns: LoRA rank sweeps measure intrinsic dimensionality only approximately; true intrinsic dimensionality uses global random projections across all parameters
Limited scope of domain generalization: Reasoning Gym results on only 4 strategies and 2 task types; unclear how cognitive/knowledge-intensive tasks relate to the core compressibility hypothesis

strengths: Strong empirical correlations (0.93 Gemma-3 4B, 0.75 1B) between intrinsic dimensionality and generalization performance across diverse CoT strategies, substantially outperforming baselines like trajectory length and KL divergence

Comprehensive experimental design spanning 14 reasoning strategies with rigorous ablations (threshold robustness in Table 3, correctness sensitivity in Table 5) and evaluation on both in-distribution and diverse OOD datasets
Clear motivation addressing a genuine gap: quantifying reasoning effectiveness beyond qualitative 'structure' arguments, with principled grounding in information theory and MDL
Reproducible methodology with detailed hyperparameters, configuration selection algorithms, extensive examples, and evaluation across two model scales
Well-structured presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-3) and honest acknowledgment of limitations
weaknesses: Critical methodological concern: LoRA provides an upper bound on intrinsic dimensionality but no validation that LoRA-based orderings preserve rankings from random projections or other methods. The theoretical justification for using LoRA rather than random projections (standard in prior work) is architectural convenience, not principled.

Circular logic and causation not established: Intrinsic dimensionality is measured on models trained with the reasoning data, then correlated with performance on that same data. This is correlational; the paper frames ID as *explaining* effectiveness but equally valid interpretation is that effective reasoning provides consistent training signals that happen to be compressible. No held-out validation of predictive power.

Threshold selection remains problematic despite robustness ablation: Absolute thresholds differ between models (24.3% vs 63.0%), and using a common threshold across strategies with different natural performance ceilings introduces bias. The justification that epoch 1 avoids overfitting is stated but not empirically validated.

Narrow scope severely limits impact: (1) Only two small model scales (1B, 4B); unclear if results generalize to 7B+ where reasoning may differ. (2) Dominated by mathematical reasoning (GSM8K); Reasoning Gym evaluation spans only 4 strategies and 2 task categories. (3) No evaluation on knowledge-intensive or retrieval tasks where CoT is known to help minimally.

Computational cost not justified: Computing ID requires 20-30 LoRA training runs per strategy; token perplexity (0.82 correlation) requires one forward pass. The 0.11 point improvement may not justify 100-1000× overhead, yet cost-benefit analysis is absent.

Limited novelty: Core contribution is applying existing intrinsic dimensionality concepts (Li et al. 2018, Aghajanyan et al. 2021) to reasoning strategies—an incremental domain transfer rather than methodological or theoretical advance. The connection to MDL is mentioned but not deeply developed.

Small sample size (n=14 strategies) limits statistical power. No confidence intervals, bootstrapped estimates, or analysis of sampling variability. Spearman correlation of 0.93 is impressive but uncertainty bounds are unknown.

No actionable insights for practitioners: Paper shows ID correlates with performance but provides no guidance on *designing* reasoning strategies to minimize ID, nor can it be used prospectively for data annotation or model selection (requires expensive post-hoc computation).

Training data confounds: Filtering by correctness causes variable dataset sizes (6.2K-7.5K). While correlation with performance is non-significant (ρ ≈ -0.11), this doesn't eliminate confounding with ID or whether controlling for fixed size would strengthen results.

Mechanistic understanding incomplete: Demonstrates correlation but limited explanation *why* low ID predicts effectiveness. Is it compressibility, output consistency, or something else? Table 5's noisy-data experiment conflates corruption with reasoning quality rather than testing hypothesis about optimal reasoning structure.

strengths: Exceptionally strong empirical correlation (0.93 for 4B model) between intrinsic dimensionality and generalization, substantially outperforming baselines like trajectory length (0.31) and KL divergence (-0.17)
Novel and principled approach grounded in information-theoretic concepts (minimum description length), providing a quantifiable alternative to qualitative explanations of reasoning effectiveness
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 14 diverse reasoning strategies, multiple model sizes (1B and 4B), in-distribution and 5 out-of-distribution test sets, plus generalization to Reasoning Gym
Thorough robustness analysis demonstrating strong correlations persist across different threshold selections (0.72-0.94), validating that findings are not artifacts of hyperparameter choices
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameter documentation, convergence analysis, dataset construction procedures, and extensive results tables in appendices
Methodologically sound use of LoRA as structured low-dimensional projection with careful justification and learning rate sweeps documented in appendices
Insightful findings: Executed PoT achieves lowest intrinsic dimensionality and best OOD performance; larger models compress effective reasoning more efficiently
weaknesses: Limited scope: primary evaluation on GSM8K (math reasoning); Reasoning Gym uses only 4 strategies vs 14 for GSM8K; generalization to other domains (coding, QA, commonsense reasoning) unclear

Only two model sizes tested (1B, 4B Gemma); the weaker correlation on 1B (0.75 vs 0.93 on 4B) suggests potential scale-dependence not fully explored; unclear if findings hold for larger models or other architectures

Computational cost not fully addressed: requires 20-30 LoRA training runs per strategy with no wall-clock timing provided; limits practical applicability for direct optimization of reasoning strategies

Causal analysis limited: while correlation is strong, the paper doesn't investigate why lower intrinsic dimensionality helps or which properties of reasoning chains drive dimensionality; lacks mechanistic understanding
LoRA used as proxy for intrinsic dimensionality without formal validation that this matches theoretical intrinsic dimensionality or Kolmogorov complexity; only LoRA tested, not other PEFT methods

Task-dependent effectiveness not adequately explained: No CoT achieves lowest dimensionality on cognitive reasoning tasks (Table 4), contradicting general pattern and suggesting metric may not be universally applicable
Data correctness sensitivity: Table 5 shows 500× increase with 50% incorrect data, but only tested at one noise level on two strategies; robustness to moderate noise levels unclear
Missing ablations: no analysis of per-dimension contributions, sensitivity to log-scale parameter sweep distribution, or how dimensionality evolves during training beyond epoch-1 and final values
Token perplexity achieves respectable 0.82 correlation; relationship and complementarity with intrinsic dimensionality not deeply explored; 'No CoT with extra tokens' control is limited
Epoch-1 training accuracy threshold is somewhat arbitrary; other threshold schemes not compared; different thresholds for different models (63% vs 24.3%) make absolute interpretation difficult
